o.text: Probably from Arabic مَا رَاقَ (mā rāqa, “what appealed to”); compare macəra. Cognate with Ottoman Turkish مراق (merak), whence Turkish merak.
Internationalism; ultimately from Ancient Greek παιδαγωγική (paidagōgikḗ).
Borrowed from Arabic أَلْوَان (ʔalwān), plural of لَوْن (lawn). The sense 'nonferrous' is a semantic loan from Russian цветной (cvetnoj).
